transcript:
This is NPR News Now, the latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Lakshmi Singh.
Republican Governor Mike DeWine of Ohio says he still supports Vivek Ramaswamy for governor,
but today DeWine urged a candidate to take down an attack ad featuring the estranged
mother of Democratic rival Amy Acton.
It was wrong to run this ad, and even at this late time, my wife Fran saw the ad run this
morning on TV, I would just urge the Ramaswamy campaign to take this down.
The ad in question features Acton's mother, Donna Arthur, calling her daughter a lifelong
liar.
However, the attack ad does not mention that Arthur's husband was charged with a raping
Acton when she was a child and that she was removed from her mother's care.
Yesterday, Vice President J.D. Vance, a former Ohio U.S. Senator, told Republicans to stop
whining about Ramaswamy's attack ad.
The U.S. and Israel are drawing up plans for another possible attack against Iran, according
to a source who spoke to NPR on condition of anonymity.
The person briefed on the war planning says it would happen after the midterms.
The U.N. Secretary General says he is heading this week to Egypt to talk about ways to tamp
down the widening wars in the region.
He's calling on countries to abide by international law and think about civilians caught up in
these conflicts.
More from NPR's Michelle Kellerman.
U.N. Secretary General Antonio Guterres says the world is already bracing for disruptive
weather patterns known as El Niño.
You are now witnessing an El Niño of war.
Conflict is feeding conflict, and the consequences are traveling farther and faster.
From the Middle East to Ukraine to Sudan, he says civilians and civilian infrastructure
have been targeted in violation of international law.
And all of this has global impacts as energy markets are disrupted, which hurts much of
the developing world.
Guterres is calling for peace, but has little time to make an impact himself.
His term ends at the end of this year.
Michelle Kellerman, NPR News, the State Department.
The Justice Department has announced a criminal indictment against a high-powered Democratic
state lawmaker in Virginia related to her family-run marijuana business.
More from NPR's Ryan Lucas.
The indictment charges 82-year-old Virginia State Senator Lily Louise Lucas with leading
a racketeering conspiracy involving marijuana distribution, money laundering, honest services
fraud and other crimes.
Six others, including several of Lucas' children, were also charged.
Attorney General Todd Blanche announced the indictment.
The charges listed in the indictment reflect the alleged behavior of a public servant who
put her own financial interests before the people she was elected to serve.
Blanche said the long-running investigation began before the Trump administration took
office.
Lucas is the president pro tempore of the Virginia Senate.
In a statement on ex, she said she will not be intimidated, and she vowed to fight the
charges.
Ryan Lucas, NPR News, Washington.
It's NPR.
The looks-maxing influencer Braden Peters, known to followers as clavicular, is pleading
not guilty to rape.
He was in court today accused of getting a 17-year-old girl drunk and then sexually assaulting
her at his family's Massachusetts home last year.
A new survey shows the monthly cost for health plans through employers in the United States
rose this year.
NPR's Selena Simmons-Duffin says the increase was about the same as inflation.
The nonpartisan health research organization KFF just released its annual survey of nearly
2,000 employers about their health benefits.
Health insurance costs have been going up fast for years.
So even though this year's increase is 5 percent, about the same as wage growth and inflation,
all those increases add up.
On average, premiums for a family of four now cost $28,000 per year, says Matthew Ray
of KFF.
"Which is just a ton of money.
It's basically the cost of a new car every year just to keep a family of four insured."
Of that total, the survey found the share that workers pay rose to more than $7,400
per year on average.
So even people with great health coverage through work are putting a lot of their income
towards health insurance.
Selena Simmons-Duffin, NPR News.
In a regulatory filing today, the medical laboratory operator Quest Diagnostics reveals
its systems were the target of a cyber attack.
Found out about it this week.
Quest Diagnostics says some of its patients' records were likely compromised.
Stocks continue to drop sharply with a Nasdaq now down 760 points.
It's NPR.
This message comes from Lisa and their lineup of beautifully crafted mattresses tailored
to how you sleep.
Go to l-e-e-s-a dot com for up to 30 percent off mattresses plus get an extra $50 off with
promo code NPR.

topics.text: Ohio Governor Mike DeWine urges Ramaswamy campaign to pull attack ad featuring Amy Acton's mother
Vance tells Republicans to stop whining about Ramaswamy's attack ad against Amy Acton
US and Israel reportedly drawing up plans for another possible attack on Iran after midterms
UN Secretary General Guterres heads to Egypt to address widening Middle East wars
Guterres warns of an 'El Niño of war' as conflicts spread across Middle East, Ukraine, Sudan
Justice Department indicts Virginia State Senator Louise Lucas over family marijuana business racketeering
Influencer Braden Peters, known as clavicular, pleads not guilty to rape charge in Massachusetts
KFF survey finds US employer health plan premiums rose 5 percent, averaging $28,000 for family of four
Quest Diagnostics discloses cyber attack that likely compromised some patients' records
